title: Quantum walker trapped by self-similarity of the Sierpiński carpet
abstract: We study the dynamics of a single quantum particle on a finite-size square lattice with a fractal structure resembling the Sierpiński carpet, and compare it to the dynamics on a uniform lattice of the same size. For a particle initially localized at a corner of the lattice, we monitor the probability of finding it near the initial and opposite corners using zone-integrated probabilities, allowing a consistent comparison across fractal orders. While on the uniform lattice the particle reaches the opposite corner ballistically, in a time proportional to the lattice size, on the Sierpiński lattice it becomes increasingly confined to the vicinity of its initial position. We show that this trapping builds up self-similarly across the whole hierarchy of corner zones of the lattice.
summary: The paper investigates how quantum walkers behave on lattices with fractal geometry, specifically the Sierpiński carpet. It shows that compared to uniform lattices where particles spread ballistically, the fractal structure causes strong, self-similar trapping near the starting point. This highlights how geometric constraints alone can suppress quantum transport.
main_problem: The study compares quantum particle transport dynamics on a fractal lattice (Sierpiński carpet) against its counterpart on a uniform lattice of the same size.
main_result: While particles move ballistically on the uniform lattice, they become increasingly trapped near their starting point on the Sierpiński carpet as the fractal order increases.
method: The dynamics are simulated by solving the time-dependent Schrödinger equation using numerical methods like Runge-Kutta, focusing on zone-integrated probabilities for comparison.
model_or_system: A single quantum particle is modeled moving via nearest-neighbor tunneling on a square lattice structure that is iteratively modified into a Sierpiński carpet fractal. The dynamics are compared against the same system on a standard uniform lattice.
key_observables: Zone-integrated probabilities for finding the particle in the initial zone ($S(t)$) versus the opposite corner zone ($F(t)$).
important_parameters: Fractal order ($R$), lattice size, and time ($t$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes continuous-time dynamics governed by nearest-neighbor tunneling only to sites belonging to the defined lattice structure.
figures_summary: Figures compare $S(t)$ and $F(t)$ for different fractal orders, showing confinement on the Sierpiński carpet versus ballistic spread on the uniform lattice. Other figures analyze the scaling of characteristic crossing times across various zone sizes ($K$).
paper_structure: The paper establishes the model by defining the dynamics on both lattices, presents key observables (zone-integrated probabilities), and then systematically compares the time evolution results to demonstrate the qualitative difference between ballistic transport and fractal trapping.
why_interesting: This work provides a clean theoretical demonstration of how geometric constraints, even without explicit disorder potentials, can fundamentally alter quantum transport properties by creating hierarchical barriers that suppress long-range coherence.
